findings.canonical_reading: VOD1 includes goblins among the Dark God's lower forces, while VOD3 presents a large independent goblin civilization/army under King Grishnak beneath Khazad-Throm.
findings.todo: Decide whether Grishnak's goblins are unrelated to the Dark God's former goblin forces, descendants/remnants of them, or part of a wider goblin people containing multiple factions. Do not assume equivalence.

findings.canonical_reading: A permanent dwarven settlement is founded in the Valley near the spring of the Silver River but receives no proper name.
findings.todo: Choose a canonical name later; use technical ID dwarven-valley-settlement until then.

findings.canonical_reading: The new joint/dwarven mine in the western mountain range is not given a proper name.
findings.todo: Choose a canonical name later; use technical ID western-dwarven-mine until then.

findings.canonical_reading: VOD3 places the dwarven settlement near the spring of the Silver River. VOD1 previously names the Rhyvall River as a major Valley trade artery and VOD2 uses Silver River.
findings.todo: Resolve the existing VOD2 TODO: determine whether Silver River and Rhyvall River are the same river, aliases, or separate rivers.

findings.canonical_reading: VOD3 again uses River City as the Valley's human trade and political center, while VOD1 names Riventhorn as a major river city.
findings.todo: Resolve the existing VOD2 TODO: determine whether River City is Riventhorn or a separate city.

findings.canonical_reading: Alaric states that the Dragon Rider Order was founded not only to protect the Valley but to defend peaceful and free peoples beyond it. VOD1 primarily describes its formation in response to the Dark God's invasion.
findings.todo: Decide whether this broader mission was part of the Order's original charter or developed later as its role expanded. The story itself need not change unless a formal founding history is later written.

findings.canonical_reading: The published story sides with Khazad-Throm against Grishnak's goblins. Drive also contains explicit alternate variants in which goblins are sympathetic and dwarves are aggressors.
findings.canon_decision: Keep all alternate moral/perspective variants as noncanonical production history unless explicitly promoted in the future.
